dependencies.title: H-CLOSE-1: stop adding when the ticker leaves the active LIP programme set
dependencies.description:
cmd/harness/run.go passes quote.MarketInput.ProgramEnded=false unconditionally, with the reasoning at the call site.

H-CLOSE-1: at end_date there is no reward left to earn, so the adding quote has no purpose; the reducing quote stays and is now genuinely free.

The naive read -- program.end_date from /incentive_programs -- is WRONG. Live universe 2026-08-07: LIP programmes are short REWARD PERIODS inside a market's life. Sampled programme KXSILVER15M-26AUG071800-00 ran start_date 21:45Z -> end_date 22:00Z on a market whose close_time was 22:00Z, while 180 of 200 active programmes sit on markets closing >24h out. So end_date passing is a gap between periods, not the end of the incentive.

The correct condition is membership: this ticker is in no active programme any more. That is a poll of /incentive_programs?status=active (public, unsigned) plus a membership test, on roughly the schedule_poll_s cadence. feed.Universe cannot answer it -- it returns {ticker: target_size} and a ticker order, and go/feed is hash-pinned.

Cost of leaving it: economic, not safety. false keeps the adding quote alive, so the failure is quoting while unpaid. Every rule bounding real exposure is wired (close lead, the operator early-close backoff, inventory ladder, gate, capital caps). The opposite error is worse: reading a between-periods gap as programme-ended stops quoting in a market that is still paying.

Title says "no composed test shows a foreign order excluding its market from

  called from startup.go:685 with PhaseStartup; fe.Exclude flows to

AND THE RESPONSE IS MIS-SPECIFIED: spec:977 (H-ORD-9) requires a GLOBAL STOP for
foreign activity discovered AFTER startup. Market exclusion is what startup
does. So this bead currently asks for the wrong behaviour to be proven.

applyRead, and latch a global stop per H-ORD-9 -- then prove it. Do NOT batch

=== 2026-08-11, RESCOPE COMPLETED (lip-7u4 final adjudication, codex directive) ===
The 2026-08-10 note above diagnosed this correctly but left the title in place.
The title is now changed to match, the type is now `bug`, and the REQUIRED
RESPONSE is pinned below -- with one part of it deliberately left open, because
the spec does not settle it and inventing an answer here would be worse than
recording the gap.

REQUIRED, and well-supported by the spec:
1. PASS PhaseLive from the live portfolio path. foreign.go:213-227's PhaseLive
   branch has zero production callers today because PhaseLive is never passed
   anywhere in the tree.
2. CONSUME eff.Foreign in applyRead. It is read nowhere in cmd/harness.
3. LATCH A DURABLE GLOBAL STOP. spec:887 -- "Foreign activity appearing *after*
   startup latches global `WINDING_DOWN`" (H-ORD-9) -- "because by then it is
   not a pre-existing condition we adopted but a live third party trading the
   account we are modelling."
4. DO NOT CANCEL THE FOREIGN ORDER. §11's F15 row (spec:1506) is explicit, and
   spec:2237 restates it: §7.5 does not cancel foreign orders, it excludes.
5. STARTUP BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED AND MUST STAY UNCHANGED. Classify at
   PhaseStartup (foreign.go:161 <- startup.go:685) -> fe.Exclude ->
   AdoptionFacts.Selected -> policy.go:170 is correct and covered. This bead
   adds the live path; it does not touch the startup one.

OPEN, AND TO BE ADJUDICATED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION -- THE SEVERITY.
The directive that prompted this rescope specified SEV1. That is an
extrapolation rather than a citation, and the tree and spec disagree with it as
written:

  - §7.5 step 5 (spec:885) gives the STARTUP foreign order `SEV2 FOREIGN_ORDER`.
  - H-ORD-9 (spec:995-999) gives `SEV1 FOREIGN_FILL` + global WINDING_DOWN to a

  - spec:887, the post-startup rule this bead implements, prescribes the global
    latch and RESTATES NO SEVERITY.
  - Today's code raises FOREIGN_ORDER SEV2 at position.go:914.
So the live foreign ORDER severity is genuinely underdetermined. The defensible
readings are (a) SEV2, consistent with every foreign-ORDER row, with the global
latch carrying the weight; or (b) SEV1, on the argument that a live third party
on the account is the same epistemic event as a foreign fill and H-ORD-9's
severity should follow the CONCLUSION rather than the artefact type. Decide
this explicitly and record the reasoning; do not let the implementation pick by
accident. The spec is SHA-pinned and must not be edited either way.

WAS: "F7 relay unproven: no composed test shows a detected host sleep forcing
resnapshot, RECONCILE_NOW and an uptime record." That framing is WRONG, and it
understates the defect by one whole category.

THIS IS NOT AN UNPROVEN RELAY. IT IS AN ABSENT ONE.
`SleepDetector` is never constructed in production. A grep for
`SleepDetector|NewSleepDetector|HOST_SLEEP` over go/ excluding _test.go returns
hits in exactly ONE file -- harness/lifecycle/sleep.go, its own definition
(type at :53, Observe at :87, the two SEV2 HOST_SLEEP_OR_STALL raises at :118
and :140, Downtime at :152). There is no caller in cmd/harness and no caller
anywhere else in the module. Nothing constructs it, so `Observe` is never
called, so HOST_SLEEP_OR_STALL can never fire on the deployed binary.

This is the same defect class as lip-lqw (inv_kill), lip-2da (stuck_s),
lip-gp8 (pnl_kill), lip-lpf (H-CAP-8) and lip-6w5 (harness/ping): a component

idle-sleeps. A sleep gap silently biases every rate, every uptime figure and
